clue.text: Place swathed in unadulterated colour

indicators.note: to be swathed in something is to be wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: unadulterated means pure, with nothing added
PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A location wrapped in pure, undiluted colour, like a room painted in one bold shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple is a hue between red and blue, so it is one example of a colour.

clue.text: Agreement about operation to reverse poverty

indicators.note: the clue asks for the whole combination to be turned round and read from the far end
about means going around, so the agreement word encloses the operation word

parts.note: yep is a casual yes, a word of agreement
a run is an operation, as in a production run or a print run

explanation.surface: A deal about a scheme meant to reverse destitution, like a government anti-poverty pact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' looks like part of the anti-poverty story, but it tells you to read the whole assembled piece backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Penury is extreme want, a synonym for being desperately poor.

clue.text: Church Father wrapped in older sheets?

indicators.note: being wrapped in something means sitting inside it, so the church and father go within the older word

parts.note: riper means more mature, older
CE is the Church of England abbreviation
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A churchman wrapped up in old bedsheets or papers, as if in ancient vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a loose one: rice paper comes in thin sheets, used in baking and for spring-roll wrappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is a thin edible material sold in flat leaves, so it can be described as sheets.

clue.text: Instrument maker stripping casing of woodwind instrument yesterday in Amiens

indicators.note: the casing is the outside, so the first and last letters of the instrument are peeled away

parts.note: a flute is a woodwind instrument
hier is French for yesterday, and Amiens is a French city

explanation.surface: An instrument maker in Amiens took the case off a woodwind instrument yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: FLUTE without its outer letters gives LUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A luthier is a craftsman who builds stringed instruments such as violins and guitars.

clue.text: Friend back in court, facing charge? Nonsense

indicators.note: in places the turned-round friend inside the court abbreviation
back means the friend word is read in reverse

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a rap is a criminal charge, as in beat the rap

explanation.surface: A friend is back in court, facing a criminal charge, and dismisses it all as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, which is to say rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: John and Mark at first become more prominent

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its first letter gives M

explanation.surface: Two Gospel writers, John and Mark, beginning to grow in stature.
explanation.walkthrough: John and Mark look like the Gospel pair; John is really a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to appear large and threatening, so to stand out or grow in importance.

clue.text: One newly famous symbol of eroticism, mostly substandard

parts.note: read as sub-standard: standard is par, and sub says the next piece sits under it in this down entry

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Venus, goddess of love, is a symbol of eroticism

explanation.surface: A newly famous person is dismissed as a sex symbol, mostly below par.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'substandard' as sub + standard: PAR is the standard, and VENU (VENUS mostly) goes under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart, someone who has suddenly risen to wealth or celebrity.

clue.text: Argues against timeless puzzle

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: rebuts means argues against or refutes

explanation.surface: Someone argues against a puzzle that has stood the test of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle in which images and letters represent words.

clue.text: Opening comments in quiet talk vaguely about energy

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: about means wrapping around, so the talk word encloses the energy letter

parts.note: to ramble is to talk at length without focus
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Introductory remarks delivered in a quiet, waffly way about energy policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is an introduction, the remarks that open a speech or document.

clue.text: University abandoning agreement about course rendered void, making particular point

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened agreement word goes around the emptied course
abandoning means the university letter leaves the agreement word

parts.note: unity means agreement or harmony

indicators.note: made void means emptied, so only the outer letters of course remain

explanation.surface: A university walks out of a deal over a cancelled course, making a pointed objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is only a link; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or subtle distinction, a precise point.

clue.text: Run into bone in pit — nasty

indicators.note: in places the run-into-bone combination inside the pit word

parts.note: a pit is a hole
R, the cricket abbreviation for run, leads straight into RIB, a bone

explanation.surface: Running into a bone in a pit sounds a nasty experience, perhaps for an archaeologist.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrible means very unpleasant, so it matches nasty as an adjective.

clue.text: Pardon Minister shedding tear about snoops mostly

indicators.note: about means the shortened minister word surrounds the snooping word
shedding means casting off, so the tear word is removed from the minister

parts.note: a minister of religion is a reverend
to rend is to tear

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: pries means snoops or noses about

explanation.surface: A government minister, no longer weeping, pardons some snoops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician but here is a clergyman, given his title.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a cancellation or postponement of punishment, as a pardon is.

clue.text: Bottle containing a lot of drink, judging by eye

indicators.note: containing means the bottle word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A bottle holding plenty of drink, its contents measured by eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual means relating to sight, so a visual estimate is one made by looking.

clue.text: Around Calais I recalled part of ship in marine debris

parts.note: around Calais they speak French, where I is je

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the ship part is read in reverse

parts.note: a mast is part of a ship

explanation.surface: Near Calais, the speaker remembers part of a ship lying among flotsam on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is goods thrown overboard that wash ashore, a kind of rubbish found at sea.

clue.text: No opening for group court case

indicators.note: no opening means the first letter of the group word is removed

parts.note: a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: A splinter group is denied access to the courts in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a lawsuit, the legal proceeding brought before a judge.

clue.text: Local government group in city beginning to heed lawyer when speaking

parts.note: Paris is a city

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: its first letter gives H

indicators.note: when speaking means the lawyer word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: counsel is a barrister or lawyer acting in a case

explanation.surface: A council in a city starts to listen to its lawyer at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNSEL (a lawyer) sounds like COUNCIL. A parish council is the smallest unit of English local government.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish council is an elected body running local affairs in an English village or parish.

clue.text: Players get disturbed about old treatment for internal problem

indicators.note: about here means on the subject of, putting the old letter ahead of the disturbance word

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show
to roil is to become turbulent or stirred up

explanation.surface: A cast of actors gets upset over an old-fashioned medicine for stomach trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: CAST, then O, then ROIL; 'old' also fits the surface, as this purgative is an old-fashioned remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor oil is a strong laxative, long given for constipation and other bowel complaints.

clue.text: School is out? Head of Physics coming in for drink

indicators.note: coming in means the physics letter goes inside the sleeping word

parts.note: someone who naps is out for the count, asleep

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter gives P

explanation.surface: School is over, so the head of physics joins in for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' looks like school breaking up but means asleep: NAPS, with P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, a kind of alcoholic beverage from Germany and Scandinavia.

clue.text: Resolved actual origins of body tissue

indicators.note: resolved means broken up and worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has resolved where something truly came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilaginous describes gristle, the firm flexible connective tissue in joints and the nose.

clue.text: Occupy hotel — soon to accept that

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the soon phrase receives the hotel letter

parts.note: in a bit means soon, shortly
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone will occupy the hotel soon and must accept what they find.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in it, taking possession as an occupant.

clue.text: Stop offering crosswords initially clued day earlier

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: its first letter gives O
its first letter gives C

indicators.note: day earlier means the D, standing for day, moves forward in the word

explanation.surface: A setter stops offering crosswords whose clues arrived a day early.
explanation.walkthrough: In CLUED the D (day) moves earlier to give CLUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or close off, as an obstruction stops a passage.

clue.text: Passionate romance enthralling Mike

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the romance word holds the Mike letter

parts.note: a romance is a story
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A passionate love affair captivates a man called Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy describes turbulent, intense feelings, as in a stormy relationship full of passion.

clue.text: Pursued switching bridge partner for nothing

indicators.note: in bridge North and South are partners, so the S compass letter is swapped for its partner N

parts.note: sought means pursued or looked for

explanation.surface: A player chased something by changing their bridge partner, all for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partnerships are North-South and East-West, so S becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought is an old word for nothing, zero.

clue.text: America, say, elevated idiom

parts.note: USA stands for the United States of America

indicators.note: elevated means raised, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: America, for instance, has an elevated way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the customary way words are used, the established idiom of a language.

clue.text: Remarkable Irish airport no longer under consideration?

parts.note: Knock is the airport in County Mayo, Ireland West Airport Knock
out means excluded, ruled out of contention

explanation.surface: An Irish airport is dropped from a shortlist, which is remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is something stunning or outstanding, as in a knockout performance.

clue.text: Circus performer of note entertaining the French

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the note encloses the French word

parts.note: fa is a note in the sol-fa scale
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A noted circus act hosting French visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Flea circuses were sideshows in which fleas were said to perform tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas were trained or shown as acts in a flea circus, making them circus artistes.

clue.text: Leeway shown by account in theatre poster

parts.note: play is slack or room to move, leeway
a bill is an account to be paid

explanation.surface: Some leeway is shown by the accounts in the running of a theatre's posters.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a printed notice advertising a stage production and its cast.

clue.text: Put up with sound of activity coming from us

parts.note: a hum is the busy murmur of activity
our means belonging to us, so coming from us

explanation.surface: We have to tolerate the noise of our own bustle.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to indulge them, going along with their wishes.

clue.text: Small muscle, nothing less — not really there at all

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: less means without, so the nothing letter is taken out

parts.note: a pectoral is a chest muscle
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A small muscle, not quite there, seems to vanish entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral means ghostly, like an apparition that seems present but has no substance.

clue.text: Theatre song gets a further look?

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A song from a show is given another look by a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a repeated showing, as when a television replay lets viewers watch again.
